object_description: two right-angled school buildings on a base above a buried sports hall
design_condition: Two school buildings are arranged at right angles to define the courtyard, while the buried sports hall and later-stage building extend the ensemble along the stream and preserve passages toward the lake landscape.

positive.statement: The compact volumes and sloping roofs seek an appropriate scale relationship with the village structure.

position.rationale: Three compact roofed volumes and their varied heights are clearly visible across plan and elevations.

positive.statement: The arrangement leaves maximum free passages and openings toward the landscape balcony.

position.target: free passages and openings toward landscape balcony
position.rationale: Open passages are legible around the courtyard and between volumes, though the balcony is not labeled.

positive.statement: The general organization is clear and functional.

position.rationale: The right-angled arrangement and connected base are directly visible in all principal views.

positive.statement: The typological quality and general compactness of the proposal are appreciated.

position.rationale: Compact grouped volumes and their typological arrangement are clearly represented.

positive.statement: The simple and rational supporting system allows great flexibility in the use and organization of the premises.

position.rationale: Structure is not separately modeled; the connected base provides a broad system anchor.

positive.statement: The proposal's rationality and simplicity are compelling.

position.rationale: The visible arrangement supports a broad architectural assessment without isolating one element.

negative.statement: The excessive multiplicity of accesses prevents a more obvious organization aligned with the requested program.

position.rationale: Individual entrances are not distinguishable; the courtyard-facing circulation zone is used as an anchor.

negative.statement: The multiplication of stairwells and generous clearance areas contradict the desired economy of means.

position.rationale: Internal circulation elements are absent; the central connected area provides a plausible constrained location.

negative.statement: The largely buried sports halls require significant earthworks and have insufficient lighting.

position.rationale: The low base extension along the lower edge best corresponds to the buried sports-hall zone.

negative.statement: The machine-room layout does not work because corridor access is difficult and the doors are substantially undersized.

position.rationale: Machine rooms are not visible; a lower service zone near the buried hall is estimated.

negative.statement: The courtyard facades lack solar protection, creating a risk of summer overheating and discomfort.

position.rationale: The courtyard is defined by the inner edges of the two right-angled school buildings.

negative.statement: The apparent simplicity is contradicted by differentiated entrances and facades with four levels on the opposite side, weakening integration with surrounding buildings.

position.rationale: The taller opposite-facing elevations and differentiated volume edges are visible, though entrances are indistinct.
